headline: All five assigned surfaces resolved. None of them is a lost venue: two (peren /static/, research.ai45) are asset/API hosts that were never publication indexes, one (robustintelligence.com) is a retired domain that 301s to Cisco, and two (llama.com/docs, openai.com/index/learning-never-stops) were readable once the client was fixed. Zero in-gap-period publications on four of the five; one dated item on the fifth.

items.title: Llama model cards and prompt formats (Llama 4, Llama Guard 4, Llama 3.3, Other models)
items.date_source: genuinely undatable - the pages carry no byline, no published/updated date and no dated changelog; the only dates anywhere in the docs corpus are 2023-07-18, 2023-12-11/12/13, 2024-01-15 and 2025-08-29 inside code samples and licence text, none of them a page date
items.rule_cited: §1 hard drop - company self-report; the company-venue test 'is an external evaluator named?' fails on every one of the four model-card pages
items.reason: Meta documenting Meta's own models. Read all four pages in full (llama4 18,127 chars; llama-guard-4 12,704; llama3_3 14,716; other-models 23,846, the last covering Llama 3, Llama Guard 2, Code Llama 70B, Llama Guard 1, Code Llama and Llama 2 inline). They are prompt-format and role/token references - introduction, architecture, prompt sections, zero-shot function-calling examples - with no evaluation results, no benchmark table and no named external evaluator anywhere; a grep for red team / third-party / independent / evaluated by / audited by / CyberSecEval / Purple Llama / MLCommons / NIST / AISI / METR / Apollo / Trail of Bits returns nothing on these pages.

items.rule_cited: §2 test 2 - operational how-to guidance, not an evidence-backed result; §1 would independently drop them as company self-report
items.reason: The remaining 29 pages of the docs tree, all read in full: overview, the model-cards index, five download/partner pages, eight how-to guides (prompting, fine-tuning, quantization, distillation, validation, vision capabilities, responsible use, overview), three integration guides and eleven deployment guides. They are instructional - how to autoscale, how to project cost, how to migrate infrastructure - and the quantitative statements in them are engineering rules of thumb (e.g. 'target a TTFT under 500ms and a generation rate of 20-50 tokens per second per user'), not measured results reported by an evaluator. No external evaluator is named on any page.

surfaces.note: TWO separate blockers, both now solved. (1) The 400 is fetch.py's header set, not Meta blocking - adding Sec-Fetch-Mode/Site/Dest/User returns 200 (independently found by agent 1; confirmed here live: 887,166 bytes). (2) Even at 200, developer.meta.com/ai/docs is a client-rendered SPA whose raw HTML contains no body text at all (298,798 bytes of the 2026-08-14 Wayback snapshot yields 0 occurrences of 'Llama 4', 'model card', 'red team' and 1 occurrence of 'Model Card'), so a 200 read of the raw HTML still looks empty. Rendering through r.jina.ai returns the real content. All 33 nav pages were fetched this way; CDX additionally shows six legacy model-card sub-pages (llama3_1, llama3_2, llama-guard-3, meta-llama-3, meta-llama-guard-2, meta-code-llama-70b, prompt-guard) whose content is reproduced inline on the 'Other models' page. www.llama.com/docs/ 301s to developer.meta.com/ai/docs/ - that migration happened between the 2026-06-05 and 2026-07-24 Wayback captures. /model-cards-and-prompt-formats/llama4_omni/ (captured 2026-08-13) is a 302 to /llama4/, not a new model card. NOTHING on this surface carries a publication date, so no page can be placed inside 2026-07-31..2026-08-29, and nothing on it names an external evaluator.

cross_agent_notes: CONFIRMED agent 1's root cause independently: adding Sec-Fetch-Mode/Site/Dest/User to fetch.py's HEADERS turns every Meta 400 into a 200 (verified live 2026-08-29: www.llama.com/docs/ 887,166 bytes, developer.meta.com/ai/docs/model-cards-and-prompt-formats/llama4/ 994,687 bytes, ai.meta.com/blog/ 209,486 bytes).

SECOND, SEPARATE META BLOCKER that a header fix alone does NOT solve: developer.meta.com/ai/docs is a client-rendered SPA. A 200 read of its raw HTML yields only the <title>. The 2026-08-14 Wayback snapshot of the model-cards index is 298,798 bytes and contains zero occurrences of 'Llama 4', 'Llama Guard', 'model card' or 'red team'. Any agent that fixes the headers and then greps the HTML will still conclude the docs are empty. They are not - render them.

GENERAL FALLBACK THAT WORKED ON FOUR SURFACES HERE: prefixing a URL with https://r.jina.ai/ returns a rendered markdown extraction and is accepted by hosts that 403 or 400 the fetcher (Meta, openai.com). It is NOT a universal key - peren.gouv.fr/static/ and research.ai45.shlab.org.cn/ both 403 through it as well, which is itself useful evidence that those denies are server-side and the paths are not pages.

WAYBACK CDX GOTCHAS hit repeatedly: (a) use https, not http - http intermittently throws ConnectionError that looks like 'CDX is down'; (b) transient ConnectionRefusedError on web.archive.org needs a retry loop, three tries with backoff was enough; (c) Wayback id_ snapshots of Meta are served content-encoding: zstd, which requests does not decode - fetch.py's _extract then returns binary garbage that scores as 'text'. Decode with the zstandard module before cleaning. Suggest adding zstd (and brotli) handling to fetch.py alongside the ContentDecodingError fix agent 3 flagged.

TWO SURFACES IN THIS PACKET ARE MISCLASSIFIED AS VENUES and should be relabelled rather than retried: www.peren.gouv.fr/static/ and research.ai45.shlab.org.cn/ are both asset hosts (the latter also a JSON API host). Neither has ever had an HTML index. Their content is fully reachable from ai45.shlab.org.cn/research/ (Hugo, with RSS) and peren.gouv.fr/en/actualites/ respectively.

ONE SURFACE IS DEAD, NOT BLOCKED: www.robustintelligence.com retired into Cisco. All 2026 Wayback captures are 301s to cisco.com/site/us/en/products/security/ai-defense/robust-intelligence-is-part-of-cisco/ and the origin now refuses TCP. Repoint the venue to blogs.cisco.com/tag/foundation-ai and blogs.cisco.com/tag/ai-defense; both are 200 direct and both top out in June 2026.

AI45 API ENDPOINTS, for anyone re-sweeping Shanghai AI Lab: https://research.ai45.shlab.org.cn/production/{BlogList,NewsList,AllNewsList,PublicationList,AllPublicationList,OperationList}.json all return 200 to a plain GET, and https://ai45.shlab.org.cn/research/index.xml (plus /research/zh/index.xml) is a real RSS feed with pubDates. Newest post on both feeds is 2026-02-10.

AGREEMENT with recovered_1.json on the Bocconi item: I recovered https://openai.com/index/what-students-gain-from-chatgpt-critical-thinking-training/ independently through the reader (5,886 chars) and both of agent 1's finding_quote strings are character-exact against my copy, as is the 2026-08-27 date. I did not duplicate the row. One note for the merge: agent 1 tiers both findings C on the ground that GPT-4o is the instrument of a human-subjects study. That is defensible, but §4's instrument exclusion sits in Gate 2 condition (c), not Gate 1, so an alternative reading is Gate 1 yes / Gate 2 no = Tier B for the access-effect row. Either way it is not Tier A; flagging it so the choice is made once rather than twice.

MY SLICE IS CLOSED: indices 1, 4, 7, 10 and 13 are all resolved with a stated mechanism. The only surface in the whole packet I would still call genuinely unread is index 3 (twitter.com/sayashk), which is agent 1's and which agent 1 also reports as not recovered.
